channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Sóstenes quer usar documentário sobre Bolsonaro para fazer campanha para Flávio
item.description: Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ), leader of the PL in the Chamber, stated at the premiere of the documentary "A Colisão dos Destinos" in Brasília that he intends to use the film about Jair Bolsonaro's political trajectory to boost the campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro, pre-candidate for President in 2026.

item.title: Cantor gospel que teve perfil suspenso por Moraes é pré-candidato a deputado federal
item.description: Gospel singer Davi Sacer announced his pre-candidacy for federal deputy in 2026 under the Progressistas (PP) party in São Paulo. His X (formerly Twitter) account was suspended in 2022 by order of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes after he posted the hotel address where Moraes and other justices were staying in New York, accompanied by a call for Brazilians to confront them. Sacer stated the suspension prompted deep reflection on freedom of expression and said his campaign is supported by family, pastors, and faith.

item.title: Ajuda de custo a paciente que se trata no SUS em outro município agora é lei
item.description: Law 15.390/2025 establishes the right to a cost allowance for SUS patients requiring out-of-municipality medical treatment (TFD), covering transportation, food, and lodging for the patient and a companion if needed. The benefit is discretionary, subject to budget availability, medical prescription, and authorization by municipal or state health managers, and does not apply to trips under 50 km or within the same metropolitan area. President Lula partially vetoed the bill, removing the provision for reimbursement of expenses if the allowance is not paid in a timely manner, citing legal uncertainty and potential increase in health-related litigation.

item.title: Alta nos preços dos combustíveis e endividamento viram munição usada pela oposição contra o governo nas redes sociais
item.description: The opposition, particularly the right, has been using rising fuel prices and growing Brazilian indebtedness as ammunition against the Lula government on social media, according to a study by Instituto Democracia em Xeque. The right accounted for 53% of tracked posts on the topic last week, compared to 29% for the left and 18% for the press. The discourse has expanded to include the impact on living costs, especially food prices, with figures like Flávio Bolsonaro and Thomas Abduch accusing the government of betraying workers and failing to deliver on promises.

item.title: Crusoé: Zema promete um novo STF
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) promised to create a 'new Supreme Federal Court' if elected, stating its members should be accountable for their actions. He presented this proposal as the first act of his future government plan in an interview released on Thursday, the 16th.

item.title: Nova lei prevê ajuda de custo para pacientes do SUS que fazem tratamento em outra cidade
item.description: Law 15.390/26 establishes cost assistance for SUS patients receiving treatment in another city, covering food, transportation, and lodging for the patient and a necessary companion. Assistance is optional, subject to budget availability, medical prescription, and health manager authorization, excluding trips under 50 km or within the same metropolitan region. President Lula vetoed reimbursement for delayed assistance, citing legal insecurity and risk of increased health-related litigation.

item.title: Lula afirma que mundo não dá direito a Trump ameaçar um país
item.description: President Lula strongly criticized Donald Trump's threats against Iran, Cuba, and Venezuela, stating that no leader has the right to undermine the sovereignty of other nations, not even the United States, and that such actions violate both the U.S. Constitution and the UN Charter. He warned that continuing this policy could lead to a third world war, which would be ten times more devastating than World War II. Lula also condemned the long-standing energy blockade against Cuba, emphasizing the importance of national sovereignty and the responsibility of major powers to uphold global peace.

item.title: Governo rejeita desoneração para compensar redução de jornada
item.description: Minister of Institutional Relations José Guimarães rejected the use of fiscal exemptions to compensate sectors affected by the reduction of the workweek from six to five days, arguing such measures failed in the past and threaten federal balance. He stated the government supports ending the 6x1 work schedule, sees congressional consensus on ending the 'inhuman schedule,' and plans to advance the debate in May, Workers' Month, via a bill or constitutional amendment, open to negotiation with a short transition period. Guimarães criticized the opposition's request for a view in the Chamber’s CCJ as evidence of lacking commitment to approving the workweek reduction.

item.title: Governo Lula adia votação do PL dos apps para depois das eleições
item.description: The Lula government postponed the vote on PLP 152/2025, which regulates app-based work, until after the October 2026 presidential elections, due to a lack of agreement between platforms, workers, and establishment owners. Despite having promised to protect delivery workers from apps like Uber, iFood, and 99, the Planalto retreated in the face of consensus impossibility, with Minister José Guimarães confirming the bill was removed from the agenda due to no agreement on any point.

item.title: Edegar Pretto (PT) anuncia que será vice de Juliana Brizola (PDT) no RS
item.description: Edegar Pretto (PT) announced he will be the running mate of Juliana Brizola (PDT) in the 2026 Rio Grande do Sul gubernatorial race, after withdrawing as a top-of-ticket candidate. The PT-PDT alliance aims to unify the left in the state and support Lula’s re-election bid, with Brizola seen as better positioned to reach a runoff.

item.title: Zema lança programa com medidas para restringir atuação do STF
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate for the Novo party, launched his government program 'Brazil Without Untouchables', proposing to restrict STF powers by requiring collegial decisions, mandating impeachment proceedings upon Senate majority, and banning relatives of justices from practicing law in courts. The plan also includes anti-corruption measures: ending privileged jurisdiction, increasing penalties for corruption crimes, and mandating full restitution of embezzled funds. Zema criticized justices Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli, saying they 'deserve prison', and cited polls showing 75% of Brazilians believe the STF has 'too much power'.

item.title: Bolsonarismo questiona nota da PF que cita 'cooperação internacional' em prisão de Ramagem nos Estados Unidos: 'Narrativa'
item.description: Allies of Jair Bolsonaro criticized the Federal Police's statement attributing Alexandre Ramagem's arrest in the U.S. to international cooperation, calling it inconsistent after his release two days later. They suggested the PF may have lied or that U.S. authorities acted improperly, challenging the official narrative. Ramagem, a fugitive in Brazil since his conviction for involvement in the coup plot, was detained by ICE on immigration-related grounds without detailed criminal charges in the U.S.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro em Pernambuco, segundo novo Datafolha
item.description: President Lula (PT) maintains a comfortable lead in voting intentions in Pernambuco, according to a new Datafolha poll released on April 16, 2026. In the first-round scenario, Lula holds 53% versus 26% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 27-point advantage. In a potential runoff, Lula reaches 59% and Bolsonaro 32%, with a margin of error of three percentage points.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro preparam seus ‘telhados de vidro’ para a campanha
item.description: The rise of Flávio Bolsonaro in polls, albeit within the margin of error, signals a highly contested 2026 election, with both candidates facing high rejection rates. Lula and Flávio are attempting to mitigate their 'glass roofs' — Lula dealing with corruption scandals involving his son and the INSS, and Flávio trying to distance himself from the 'rachadinha' allegedly orchestrated by his former chief of staff. Meanwhile, the Banco Master case and ongoing plea bargains threaten to impact both sides, with each attempting to blame the crisis on the previous administration.

item.title: Além de Wagner Moura, os brasileiros que já foram capa da revista Time
item.description: The article lists Brazilians who have appeared on the cover of Time magazine, from Afrânio do Amaral in 1929 to Wagner Moura in 2026. It includes presidents such as Getúlio Vargas and Lula, scientists, diplomats, and indigenous activists, highlighting their global impact. The most recent entry is Wagner Moura, recognized for his role in O Agente Secreto and international cultural influence.

item.title: Ministro de Lula fala em elevar dívida para proteger economia popular
item.description: Minister José Guimarães stated the government may increase public debt to protect the popular economy amid U.S. tariff war effects, citing existing measures like diesel subsidies and federal tax cuts, and announced upcoming actions on gasoline, fertilizers, and household debt. He also noted congressional majority support for regulating online betting, despite President Lula’s opposition.

item.title: “Se a eleição fosse domingo, ele venceria no 1º turno”, diz diretor do Paraná Pesquisas sobre Tarcísio
item.description: According to Murilo Hidalgo of Paraná Pesquisas, Tarcísio de Freitas would win in the first round if the election were held today, with 47.8% voting intention versus 33.1% for Fernando Haddad. His advantage stems from low rejection, consistent performance across all voter demographics, and strong personal image, making a runoff unlikely.

item.title: Guimarães diz ser contra socorro do governo ao BRB
item.description: Minister José Guimarães declared he is radically opposed to any federal government bailout of the BRB, the Distrito Federal’s public bank involved in the Banco Master case, stating that those responsible must be punished and that this aligns with President Lula’s position. The remarks were made during a press briefing at the Palácio do Planalto, following the arrest of former BRB president Paulo Henrique Costa in the fourth phase of Operation Compliance Zero, which investigates unfounded operations and governance failures.

item.title: A alfinetada de ministro de Lula à performance de Flávio Bolsonaro nas pesquisas
item.description: A alfinetada de ministro de Lula à performance de Flávio Bolsonaro nas pesquisas

item.title: Zema diz que levará candidatura até o fim, alfineta Flávio e Caiado e propõe reforma no STF
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), former governor of Minas Gerais, stated he will maintain his presidential pre-candidacy even if invited to be Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) running mate, adding that his first measure if elected would be a reform of the STF (Supreme Federal Court). He criticized Flávio Bolsonaro and Governor Ronaldo Caiado (União Brasil) for their political stances, emphasizing his independence and liberal agenda.

item.title: Judeus não-sionistas acusam assessora de Lula de censurá-los em evento
item.description: Brazilian Jewish organizations claimed that Lula’s special advisor, Clara Ant, blocked their participation in the government-organized seminar 'Combating Antisemitism' in Brasília, accusing her of censorship. The incident occurred this week and sparked controversy over freedom of expression in official events addressing antisemitism.

item.title: Corte italiana se manifesta a favor extradição de Zambelli
item.description: Italy's Appeals Court ruled in favor of the extradition of Carla Zambelli to Brazil, where she is accused of chasing a man with a firearm in São Paulo during the 2022 elections. This marks the second favorable ruling by Italian courts on her extradition; Zambelli has been detained in Rome's Rebibbia female prison since June 2025 following a Supreme Court conviction for illegal firearm possession and illegal coercion.

item.title: Alerj: oposição ao PL combina retirada caso votação para presidência seja aberta
item.description: Opposition party leaders in the Alerj met to define strategy for tomorrow's vote on the presidency of the House, advocating for secret voting and threatening to withdraw from the plenary if the vote is open. The coalition, including PSD, MDB, Podemos, PT, PDT, PSB, Cidadania, PCdoB and PV, is backing a single candidate, Vitor Junior (PDT), endorsed by Eduardo Paes (PSD), while PSOL did not sign the statement and may field its own candidate. The bloc estimates 25–27 votes—below the 36 needed—and awaits a judicial ruling on voting format, with actions filed at the STF and TJ-RJ to secure secret voting.

item.title: Frente partidária ameaça deixar plenário da Alerj se eleição para presidência mantiver voto aberto
item.description: Nine parties allied with Eduardo Paes threaten to walk out of the Alerj plenary if the presidency vote is conducted by open ballot, claiming it exposes lawmakers to pressure and coercion. The bloc advocates for secret voting to protect legislative independence and supports Vitor Junior (PDT) as their candidate. The PL, with 23 deputies plus allies from União Brasil and PP, would have a guaranteed majority in an open vote to elect Douglas Ruas, while the PDT has filed a lawsuit with the TJ-RJ to ensure a secret ballot.

item.title: ‘Eu não vim para cá para ser um Zé Mané’, diz Guimarães, novo ministro da articulação política
item.description: The new Minister of Institutional Relations, José Guimarães, admitted that the Lula government suffers from a lack of unity in political articulation with Congress and said he aims to change this situation, emphasizing the need to build consensus amid disagreement. He cited stalled issues such as the Public Security PEC, the Redata tax regime, the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, and the app-based work regulation bill, all blocked in the Senate, and pledged to engage with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Guimarães also dismissed Flávio Bolsonaro’s polling competitiveness, stating that 'the time will come for the jaguar to drink water'.

item.title: Zema nega ser vice de Flávio Bolsonaro e diz que vai levar candidatura presidencial até o fim
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for President from the Novo Party, denied he intends to be Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate and said he will maintain his presidential candidacy until the end of the 2026 elections. At an event in São Paulo, he unveiled his government plan, highlighting proposals such as broad privatization, reducing the age of criminal responsibility to 16, creating a parallel labor category to CLT, and integrating agriculture with environmental policies. Zema also defended his 2023 salary increase as governor, stating he donates the entire amount to charity and that prior to his administration, secretaries earned more.

item.title: Fachin evita confronto direto, mas desafia ala que quer um STF mais ‘combativo’
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin avoided direct confrontation with colleagues demanding a more assertive public defense of the Court, maintaining his focus on judicial agenda over public statements. Despite quiet criticism from ministers including Flávio Dino, Cristiano Zanin, Gilmar Mendes, Alexandre de Moraes, and Dias Toffoli over his delayed response to the indictment of colleagues in the Senate’s Organized Crime CPI, Fachin insisted the Court’s defense lies in high-impact rulings and expediting monocractic decisions, not in media engagements.

item.title: A preocupação de novo ministro da articulação política sobre a relação com o Congresso
item.description: Newly appointed Minister of Institutional Relations José Guimarães stated that improving the federal government’s relationship with Congress is a top priority to advance key legislative proposals. He emphasized the need to strengthen dialogue with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, whose relationship with President Lula has been strained since Lula nominated Jorge Messias to the STF instead of Alcolumbre’s preferred candidate, Rodrigo Pacheco. Guimarães confirmed that talks have begun and stressed that honoring agreements is the most cost-effective political strategy to move the government’s agenda forward.

item.title: Comissão aprova projeto que classifica honorários de advogados como verba alimentar
item.description: The Constitution, Justice and Citizenship Committee (CCJ) of the Chamber of Deputies approved Bill 850/23, which amends the Statute of the OAB to classify lawyers' fees as alimentary credits, meaning they cannot be seized and must be prioritized in payments, including in bankruptcy or judicial recovery. The measure aligns with prior rulings by the STF and STJ and was approved with a favorable report by Deputy Maria Arraes (PSB-PE), who rejected Bill 8595/17 and other attached texts. The bill will now go to presidential sanction unless challenged for a plenary vote.

item.title: Novo ministro diz que governo tomará mais medidas para evitar efeitos da guerra e diz que regulação de trabalho por app fica para depois das eleições
item.description: Minister of Institutional Relations José Guimarães said the government will soon announce additional economic measures to counter the impact of the Middle East war on fuel prices, noting current actions are insufficient. He also stated that regulation of app-based work will be postponed until after the elections due to lack of alignment among Congress, government, and companies, and advocated for repealing the 'blusinhas tax' on small imports, which he believes harms President Lula’s image.

item.title: Datafolha diz que 53% defendem ida de Neymar para Copa 2026
item.description: A Datafolha survey from April 2025 shows 53% of Brazilians support Neymar's call-up for the 2026 World Cup, up from 48% in June 2025. Support is higher among Flávio Bolsonaro voters (62%) and lower among Lula supporters (46%). Coach Carlo Ancelotti has not called up Neymar since taking office.

item.title: TSE mantém desaprovação de contas de prefeito e vice de Teotônio Vilela (AL)
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the rejection of the campaign accounts of the elected mayor and vice-mayor of Teotônio Vilela (AL), Pedro Henrique de Jesus Pereira and André Borges Pereira da Silva, due to irregularities in the use of FEFC funds. The decision confirms the ruling of the Regional Electoral Court of Alagoas (TRE-AL), which ordered the return of R$ 93.337,37 to the National Treasury. The defense argued the flaws were merely formal, but the TSE rejected the appeal, maintaining the obligation to repay.

item.title: Empresários se mobilizam contra possível fim da taxa das blusinhas: 'Medida eleitoreira'
item.description: Business leaders and workers from 67 associations protested the potential repeal of the 'blusinhas tax,' calling it an electoral maneuver and advocating for continued taxation on low-value imports to ensure fiscal fairness and protect domestic industry. They argue that ending the tax would not attract new investment, as foreign platforms have invested little in Brazil despite generating R$ 40 billion in revenue between 2023 and 2025, and that the Remessa Conforme program has already boosted employment and tax collection. The government is split, with the Finance and Development, Industry and Trade ministries opposing the repeal, while the political faction supports it to improve Lula’s popularity.

item.title: Justiça nega pedido de suspensão e libera eleição da Alerj marcada para sexta-feira; entenda
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice rejected a request to suspend the election for the presidency of the State Legislative Assembly (Alerj), keeping the vote scheduled for Friday, the 17th. The ruling upheld legislative autonomy and affirmed that acting Governor Ricardo Couto must remain in office until the STF defines the format of the interim mandate. The election follows the annulment of a prior attempt and the TSE’s recount of 2022 votes, which could alter the Assembly’s composition.

item.title: Petista confirma vice na chapa de Juliana Brizola (PDT) ao governo do RS
item.description: Edegar Pretto (PT) announced he will be the vice-gubernatorial candidate on Juliana Brizola's (PDT) ticket for the Rio Grande do Sul government, following national PT coordination to support Lula's pre-campaign. The alliance aims to present a 'better project' for the state, committed to democracy, social justice, and development, despite historical tensions between the PT and PDT in RS.

item.title: MP inclui classe média no Minha Casa, Minha Vida
item.description: Provisional Measure 1.350/2026 expands access to the Minha Casa, Minha Vida housing program to families earning up to R$13,000 per month, including income brackets III and IV, previously excluded. The FGHab guaranty fund covers loan payments in case of default, reducing bank risk and enabling lower interest rates, especially for lower-income brackets. The measure is already in effect but must be approved by Congress within 120 days to become permanent law.

item.title: Lula viaja à Europa e Alckmin assume Presidência
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva traveled to Europe on Thursday (April 16, 2026) for a six-day agenda in Spain, Germany, and Portugal, aiming to consolidate partnerships, attract investments, and discuss global issues such as democracy and multilateralism. During his absence, Vice President Geraldo Alckmin assumes the Presidency of Brazil. The trip takes place two weeks before the entry into force of the Mercosul-European Union agreement, scheduled for May 1, 2026.

item.title: Silvia Abravanel atenua críticas de Zezé di Camargo contra SBT
item.description: Silvia Abravanel, daughter of Silvio Santos, commented on Zezé di Camargo's criticism of Lula and authorities appearing on SBT, stating that his opinion must be respected as part of democracy, even if not shared. She noted that her sisters chose to involve the legal team to handle the matter, leaving judicial evaluation to Zezé's statements. Silvia also promoted her weekly show on the GENTE column, available on streaming platforms and podcast.

item.title: Marinho critica troca de membros em CPI e defende rejeição de indicado ao STF
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho criticized the change in the composition of the Organized Crime CPI, stating that the last-minute substitution of members interfered with the outcome and parliamentary freedom. He defended rapporteur Alessandro Vieira and argued that the Senate must reject Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, claiming it would undermine the independence of the branches and the credibility of the Supreme Court.

item.title: Tarcísio nomeia primeira mulher para chefiar a Polícia Militar de SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas appointed Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli as the first woman to lead the state's Military Police, nearly 200 years after its founding in 1831. Cavalli, 50, has a distinguished career in the force, holding degrees in Law and Physical Education, plus a master's and doctorate in Police Sciences. Her appointment comes amid rising femicide rates in the state and the case of soldier Gisele Alves Santana, whose death was attributed to her husband, Lieutenant Colonel Geraldo Neto.

item.title: Todas as críticas ácidas de Lula contra Trump em entrevista franca ao ‘El País’
item.description: Lula sharply criticized Donald Trump in an interview with El País, accusing him of acting childishly and threatening countries without legitimacy, arguing that two 80-year-old leaders should engage with maturity and respect, not fear. He also questioned the credibility of the United Nations, stating that without reform, Trump’s criticisms would be valid, and condemned the U.S. attack on Iran as a strategic error that ignores global consequences and violates other nations’ sovereignty.

item.title: Sem Michelle, Valdemar cancela evento do PL Mulher no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto canceled the PL Women’s event in Rio de Janeiro scheduled for April 17–18 due to Michelle Bolsonaro’s absence, as she has stepped back from party activities to care for jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest. The cancellation was framed as a necessary act of respect and priority for Bolsonaro’s health, with a new date to be announced. The move raises concerns about how Michelle’s absence may affect Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential campaign, given her prominence in the party.

item.title: BR-319: ambientalistas vão à Justiça contra governo Lula por uso de dispositivo, antes vetado pelo presidente, para avançar editais
item.description: Environmentalists from the Observatório do Clima announce a Civil Public Action against the Lula government's bidding documents for the BR-319 highway repaving, claiming the use of a device previously vetoed by Lula himself in the Environmental Licensing Law and later reinstated by Congress. The bids, totaling over R$1.3 billion, allegedly violate the Constitution and pose significant risks to Amazon deforestation control, particularly in the middle stretch between km 250.7 and 590.1. Bid opening is scheduled for April 29 and 30.

item.title: Tarcísio é aprovado por 64,9% em São Paulo, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on April 16, 2026 shows that Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has 64.9% approval in São Paulo, with 31.4% disapproval. His government is rated as excellent or good by 47.3% of voters, while 22.6% consider it bad or terrible. The survey, registered with the TSE under SP-00378/2026, interviewed 1,600 people between April 11–14, with a 2.5-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Esposa de Ramagem publica vídeo de reencontro após prisão pelo ICE nos EUA
item.description: Rebeca Ramagem shared a video showing her reunion with her husband, Alexandre Ramagem, after his release from U.S. immigration detention by ICE over irregular migration status. He had been detained two days earlier after entering the U.S. irregularly, using an expired tourist visa and a canceled diplomatic passport, following his flight from Brazil amid a conviction and extradition request by the STF. In her caption, she emphasized family resilience and faith in justice, tying the moment to her husband’s ongoing legal struggle.

item.title: Quem é coronel Glauce, 1ª mulher a chefiar a PM de SP em 200 anos
item.description: Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli has been appointed by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas as the first woman to command the Military Police of São Paulo in nearly 200 years, as published in the State Official Gazette. Her career features advanced academic training (master’s and doctorate in Police Sciences), degrees in Law and Physical Education, and extensive experience in logistics, legal affairs, social communication, and operational leadership of key units in the capital. The government praised her technical excellence, recognized leadership, and readiness to lead the nation’s largest police force.

item.title: Maioria dos brasileiros querem Neymar na Copa de 2026, diz pesquisa Datafolha
item.description: A recent Datafolha poll shows 53% of Brazilians want Neymar included in Brazil’s 2026 World Cup squad, compared to 34% opposed and 8% indifferent. Despite public support, the 34-year-old striker struggles with recurring physical issues and inconsistent performance since a serious knee injury in October 2023. His return to Santos in early 2025 aims to regain fitness and national team selection ahead of Ancelotti’s final roster announcement on May 18.

item.title: Após embates com Trump, Pedro Sánchez ganha influência na esquerda global
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez strengthens his global influence by hosting the Global Progressive Mobilization summit in Barcelona, bringing together progressive leaders including Brazil's Lula da Silva. His confrontational stance toward the U.S. and Israel — labeling the Gaza war as genocide and rejecting Trump’s demand to raise defense spending to 5% of GDP — has positioned him as a leading Western voice opposing Trump’s policies, despite domestic challenges including political polarization and corruption scandals involving his allies.

item.title: Os disparos de Lula contra Trump, Milei e a ONU em entrevista ao El País
item.description: Lula sharply criticized Donald Trump’s foreign policy, stating the U.S. president has no right to threaten other countries and that the UN lacks the power to maintain peace. He dismissed concerns about Argentine President Javier Milei, saying he has no relationship or interest in engaging with him, and called for UN Security Council reform, including abolishing the veto and adding permanent members such as Brazil, India, Germany, and African nations.

item.title: Inteligência artificial liga alerta a seis meses das eleições
item.description: Six months before the 2026 elections, AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini continue violating TSE norms by providing political rankings and opinions, despite March restrictions. They name Tarcísio de Freitas and Romeu Zema as the 'best technically,' while Lula receives mixed evaluations and Flávio Bolsonaro is marginalized or omitted. This raises concerns about algorithmic bias and disinformation contaminating the electoral process.
